prompt: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare co-purchase patterns across store locations and seasonal periods to reveal location- and season-specific buying behavior.
title: Co-Purchase Bundle Analysis
summary: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare co-purchase patterns across store locations and seasonal periods to reveal location- and season-specific buying behavior.
executed_sql_queries:
WITH dedup_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.order_id,
        oi.product_id,
        oi.quantity,
        oi.unit_price,
        oi.discount_percent,
        oi.discount_amount,
        oi.total_amount
    FROM retail.order_items oi
), order_totals AS (
    SELECT
        order_id,
        SUM(total_amount) AS order_total_amount,
        COUNT(*) AS line_item_rows,
        COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS distinct_products
    FROM dedup_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.store_id,
    o.order_date,
    ot.order_total_amount,
    ot.line_item_rows,
    ot.distinct_products
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN order_totals ot
    ON o.order_id = ot.order_id
ORDER BY o.order_id
LIMIT 20;

WITH order_seasons AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    o.order_date,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'winter'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'spring'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'summer'
      ELSE 'fall'
    END AS season
  FROM retail.orders o
),
dedup_items AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, oi.product_id
  FROM retail.order_items oi
)
SELECT
  os.season,
  COUNT(DISTINCT os.order_id) AS order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT di.product_id) AS distinct_products_in_orders
FROM order_seasons os
JOIN dedup_items di
  ON os.order_id = di.order_id
GROUP BY os.season
ORDER BY os.season;

WITH order_seasons AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'winter'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'spring'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'summer'
      ELSE 'fall'
    END AS season
  FROM retail.orders o
),
dedup_items AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oi.order_id,
    oi.product_id,
    oi.total_amount
  FROM retail.order_items oi
),
season_items AS (
  SELECT
    os.season,
    di.order_id,
    di.product_id,
    di.total_amount
  FROM order_seasons os
  JOIN dedup_items di
    ON os.order_id = di.order_id
),
season_order_counts AS (
  SELECT season, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders
  FROM season_items
  GROUP BY season
),
pair_orders AS (
  SELECT
    a.season,
    a.order_id,
    a.product_id AS product_id_1,
    b.product_id AS product_id_2,
    SUM(a.total_amount + b.total_amount) AS pair_basket_value
  FROM season_items a
  JOIN season_items b
    ON a.season = b.season
   AND a.order_id = b.order_id
   AND a.product_id < b.product_id
  GROUP BY a.season, a.order_id, a.product_id, b.product_id
),
pair_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    po.season,
    po.product_id_1,
    po.product_id_2,
    COUNT(DISTINCT po.order_id) AS co_purchase_frequency,
    AVG(po.pair_basket_value) AS average_basket_value_contribution
  FROM pair_orders po
  GROUP BY po.season, po.product_id_1, po.product_id_2
),
product_season_counts AS (
  SELECT
    season,
    product_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS product_order_count
  FROM season_items
  GROUP BY season, product_id
)
SELECT
  pm.season,
  p1.product_name AS product_name_1,
  p2.product_name AS product_name_2,
  pm.co_purchase_frequency,
  ROUND(pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / soc.total_orders, 6) AS support,
  ROUND(pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / soc.total_orders, 6) AS share_of_orders,
  ROUND(pm.average_basket_value_contribution, 2) AS average_basket_value_contribution,
  ROUND(pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / soc.total_orders, 6) AS unique_order_count,
  ROUND(pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / NULLIF(ps1.product_order_count, 0), 6) AS confidence_product1_to_product2,
  ROUND(pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / NULLIF(ps2.product_order_count, 0), 6) AS confidence_product2_to_product1,
  ROUND((pm.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / soc.total_orders) /
        NULLIF((ps1.product_order_count::numeric / soc.total_orders) * (ps2.product_order_count::numeric / soc.total_orders), 0), 6) AS lift
FROM pair_metrics pm
JOIN season_order_counts soc
  ON pm.season = soc.season
JOIN product_season_counts ps1
  ON pm.season = ps1.season AND pm.product_id_1 = ps1.product_id
JOIN product_season_counts ps2
  ON pm.season = ps2.season AND pm.product_id_2 = ps2.product_id
JOIN retail.products p1
  ON pm.product_id_1 = p1.product_id
JOIN retail.products p2
  ON pm.product_id_2 = p2.product_id
ORDER BY pm.season, pm.co_purchase_frequency DESC, p1.product_name, p2.product_name
LIMIT 40;

SELECT store_id, store_name, is_online FROM retail.stores WHERE store_name IN ('Zava Retail Seattle','Zava Retail Bellevue','Zava Retail Tacoma','Zava Retail Spokane','Zava Retail Everett','Zava Retail Redmond','Zava Retail Kirkland','Zava Retail Online') ORDER BY store_name;

WITH store_map AS (
  SELECT store_id, store_name
  FROM retail.stores
  WHERE store_name IN ('Zava Retail Seattle','Zava Retail Bellevue','Zava Retail Tacoma','Zava Retail Spokane','Zava Retail Everett','Zava Retail Redmond','Zava Retail Kirkland','Zava Retail Online')
)
SELECT sm.store_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS distinct_orders,
       COUNT(*) AS order_rows,
       MIN(o.order_date) AS first_order_date,
       MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order_date
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN store_map sm ON sm.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY sm.store_name
ORDER BY sm.store_name;

SELECT o.store_id,
       s.store_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS distinct_orders,
       MIN(o.order_date) AS first_order_date,
       MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order_date
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE s.store_name IN ('Zava Retail Seattle','Zava Retail Bellevue','Zava Retail Tacoma','Zava Retail Spokane','Zava Retail Everett','Zava Retail Redmond','Zava Retail Kirkland','Zava Retail Online')
GROUP BY o.store_id, s.store_name
ORDER BY s.store_name;

WITH base_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.order_id,
        oi.product_id,
        p.product_name,
        o.store_id,
        s.store_name,
        o.order_date,
        CASE
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'winter'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'spring'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'summer'
            ELSE 'fall'
        END AS season
    FROM retail.order_items oi
    JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
), order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(total_amount) AS order_total
    FROM retail.order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
), pair_orders AS (
    SELECT
        a.store_name,
        a.season,
        a.product_id AS product_id_1,
        a.product_name AS product_name_1,
        b.product_id AS product_id_2,
        b.product_name AS product_name_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS co_purchase_frequency,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM base_items a
    JOIN base_items b
      ON a.order_id = b.order_id
     AND a.product_id < b.product_id
    GROUP BY a.store_name, a.season, a.product_id, a.product_name, b.product_id, b.product_name
), pair_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        po.*,
        COUNT(DISTINCT bi.order_id) FILTER (WHERE bi.product_id = po.product_id_1) AS orders_with_product_1,
        COUNT(DISTINCT bi.order_id) FILTER (WHERE bi.product_id = po.product_id_2) AS orders_with_product_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT bi.order_id) AS total_orders_segment
    FROM pair_orders po
    JOIN base_items bi
      ON bi.store_name = po.store_name
     AND bi.season = po.season
    GROUP BY po.store_name, po.season, po.product_id_1, po.product_name_1, po.product_id_2, po.product_name_2, po.co_purchase_frequency, po.order_count
), pair_final AS (
    SELECT
        pm.store_name,
        pm.season,
        pm.product_name_1,
        pm.product_name_2,
        pm.co_purchase_frequency,
        pm.order_count,
        ROUND(100.0 * pm.order_count / NULLIF(pm.total_orders_segment,0), 2) AS share_of_orders,
        ROUND(1.0 * pm.order_count / NULLIF(pm.total_orders_segment,0), 6) AS support,
        ROUND(1.0 * pm.order_count / NULLIF(pm.orders_with_product_1,0), 6) AS confidence_product_1_to_2,
        ROUND(1.0 * pm.order_count / NULLIF(pm.orders_with_product_2,0), 6) AS confidence_product_2_to_1,
        ROUND((1.0 * pm.order_count / NULLIF(pm.total_orders_segment,0)) /
              NULLIF((1.0 * pm.orders_with_product_1 / NULLIF(pm.total_orders_segment,0)) * (1.0 * pm.orders_with_product_2 / NULLIF(pm.total_orders_segment,0)),0), 6) AS lift,
        ROUND(AVG(ot.order_total), 2) AS average_basket_value_contribution
    FROM pair_metrics pm
    JOIN base_items bi
      ON bi.store_name = pm.store_name
     AND bi.season = pm.season
    JOIN order_totals ot
      ON ot.order_id = bi.order_id
    GROUP BY pm.store_name, pm.season, pm.product_name_1, pm.product_name_2, pm.co_purchase_frequency, pm.order_count, pm.total_orders_segment, pm.orders_with_product_1, pm.orders_with_product_2
), bundle_orders AS (
    SELECT
        a.store_name,
        a.season,
        a.product_id AS product_id_1,
        a.product_name AS product_name_1,
        b.product_id AS product_id_2,
        b.product_name AS product_name_2,
        c.product_id AS product_id_3,
        c.product_name AS product_name_3,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS unique_order_count
    FROM base_items a
    JOIN base_items b
      ON a.order_id = b.order_id
     AND a.product_id < b.product_id
    JOIN base_items c
      ON a.order_id = c.order_id
     AND b.product_id < c.product_id
    GROUP BY a.store_name, a.season, a.product_id, a.product_name, b.product_id, b.product_name, c.product_id, c.product_name
), bundle_final AS (
    SELECT
        bo.store_name,
        bo.season,
        bo.product_name_1,
        bo.product_name_2,
        bo.product_name_3,
        bo.unique_order_count,
        ROUND(1.0 * bo.unique_order_count / NULLIF(seg.total_orders_segment,0), 6) AS support,
        ROUND(100.0 * bo.unique_order_count / NULLIF(seg.total_orders_segment,0), 2) AS share_of_orders
    FROM bundle_orders bo
    JOIN (
        SELECT store_name, season, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders_segment
        FROM base_items
        GROUP BY store_name, season
    ) seg
      ON seg.store_name = bo.store_name AND seg.season = bo.season
)
SELECT 'pair' AS bundle_type, *
FROM (
    SELECT store_name, season, product_name_1, product_name_2, NULL::text AS product_name_3,
           co_purchase_frequency, order_count, share_of_orders, support,
           confidence_product_1_to_2 AS confidence, lift, average_basket_value_contribution,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY store_name, season ORDER BY co_purchase_frequency DESC, lift DESC) AS rn
    FROM pair_final
) x
WHERE rn <= 10
UNION ALL
SELECT 'bundle' AS bundle_type, *
FROM (
    SELECT store_name, season, product_name_1, product_name_2, product_name_3,
           unique_order_count AS co_purchase_frequency, unique_order_count AS order_count, share_of_orders, support,
           NULL::numeric AS confidence, NULL::numeric AS lift, NULL::numeric AS average_basket_value_contribution,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY store_name, season ORDER BY unique_order_count DESC) AS rn
    FROM bundle_final
) y
WHERE rn <= 10
ORDER BY bundle_type, store_name, season, co_purchase_frequency DESC;

WITH base_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.order_id,
        oi.product_id,
        p.product_name,
        o.store_id,
        s.store_name,
        o.order_date,
        CASE
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'winter'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'spring'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'summer'
            ELSE 'fall'
        END AS season
    FROM retail.order_items oi
    JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
), segment_orders AS (
    SELECT store_name, season, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders
    FROM base_items
    GROUP BY store_name, season
), pair_counts AS (
    SELECT
        a.store_name,
        a.season,
        a.product_id AS product_id_1,
        a.product_name AS product_name_1,
        b.product_id AS product_id_2,
        b.product_name AS product_name_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS co_purchase_frequency
    FROM base_items a
    JOIN base_items b
      ON a.order_id = b.order_id
     AND a.product_id < b.product_id
    GROUP BY a.store_name, a.season, a.product_id, a.product_name, b.product_id, b.product_name
), pair_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        pc.*,
        so.total_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bi.product_id = pc.product_id_1 THEN bi.order_id END) AS orders_with_product_1,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bi.product_id = pc.product_id_2 THEN bi.order_id END) AS orders_with_product_2
    FROM pair_counts pc
    JOIN base_items bi
      ON bi.store_name = pc.store_name
     AND bi.season = pc.season
    JOIN segment_orders so
      ON so.store_name = pc.store_name
     AND so.season = pc.season
    GROUP BY pc.store_name, pc.season, pc.product_id_1, pc.product_name_1, pc.product_id_2, pc.product_name_2, pc.co_purchase_frequency, so.total_orders
)
SELECT
    store_name,
    season,
    product_name_1,
    product_name_2,
    co_purchase_frequency,
    ROUND(1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0), 6) AS support,
    ROUND(100.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0), 2) AS share_of_orders,
    ROUND(1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(orders_with_product_1,0), 6) AS confidence_product_1_to_2,
    ROUND(1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(orders_with_product_2,0), 6) AS confidence_product_2_to_1,
    ROUND((1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0)) /
          NULLIF((1.0 * orders_with_product_1 / NULLIF(total_orders,0)) * (1.0 * orders_with_product_2 / NULLIF(total_orders,0)),0), 6) AS lift
FROM pair_metrics
ORDER BY co_purchase_frequency DESC, lift DESC
LIMIT 50;

WITH base_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.order_id,
        oi.product_id,
        p.product_name,
        o.store_id,
        s.store_name,
        o.order_date,
        CASE
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'winter'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'spring'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'summer'
            ELSE 'fall'
        END AS season
    FROM retail.order_items oi
    JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
), order_stats AS (
    SELECT order_id, store_name, season, COUNT(*) AS distinct_products
    FROM base_items
    GROUP BY order_id, store_name, season
), segment_orders AS (
    SELECT store_name, season, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
    FROM order_stats
    GROUP BY store_name, season
), pair_orders AS (
    SELECT
        a.store_name,
        a.season,
        a.product_name AS product_name_1,
        b.product_name AS product_name_2,
        COUNT(*) AS co_purchase_frequency
    FROM base_items a
    JOIN base_items b
      ON a.order_id = b.order_id
     AND a.product_id < b.product_id
    GROUP BY a.store_name, a.season, a.product_name, b.product_name
), pair_enriched AS (
    SELECT
        po.store_name,
        po.season,
        po.product_name_1,
        po.product_name_2,
        po.co_purchase_frequency,
        so.total_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bi.product_name = po.product_name_1 THEN bi.order_id END) AS orders_with_product_1,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bi.product_name = po.product_name_2 THEN bi.order_id END) AS orders_with_product_2
    FROM pair_orders po
    JOIN base_items bi
      ON bi.store_name = po.store_name
     AND bi.season = po.season
    JOIN segment_orders so
      ON so.store_name = po.store_name
     AND so.season = po.season
    GROUP BY po.store_name, po.season, po.product_name_1, po.product_name_2, po.co_purchase_frequency, so.total_orders
)
SELECT
    store_name,
    season,
    product_name_1,
    product_name_2,
    co_purchase_frequency,
    ROUND(1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0), 6) AS support,
    ROUND(100.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0), 2) AS share_of_orders,
    ROUND(1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(orders_with_product_1,0), 6) AS confidence,
    ROUND((1.0 * co_purchase_frequency / NULLIF(total_orders,0)) /
          NULLIF((1.0 * orders_with_product_1 / NULLIF(total_orders,0)) * (1.0 * orders_with_product_2 / NULLIF(total_orders,0)),0), 6) AS lift
FROM pair_enriched
ORDER BY co_purchase_frequency DESC, lift DESC
LIMIT 25;

components.content:
Executive summary: In the accessible store set, only Zava Retail Seattle (store_id 1) returned order rows, with 54,931 distinct orders spanning 2020-01-01 to 2026-12-31. Seasonal demand is very even, ranging from 13,572 fall orders to 14,041 winter orders, so bundle opportunities are not being driven by a single season.

Strongest bundle opportunities overall come from pairs with both high co-purchase frequency and very strong lift. The most compelling combinations in the retrieved seasonal results are:

  • Scrolling Jigsaw + Fixed Base Router 1-3/4 HP — 9 co-purchases, lift 23.18, and the highest average basket value contribution among the top pairs at $507.45.
  • Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Adjustable Wrench 10-inch — 11 co-purchases, lift 22.48, average basket value contribution $103.32.
  • GFCI Outlet 20-Amp + Retractable Cord Reel — 9 co-purchases, lift 22.45, average basket value contribution $164.30.
  • PVC Pipe 3-inch x 10ft + Copper Pipe 1/2-inch Type L — 9 co-purchases, lift 22.03, average basket value contribution $148.07.
  • Adjustable Wrench 10-inch + SAE Hex Key Set — 10 co-purchases, lift 21.75, average basket value contribution $78.15.

Best volume + value balance: Torque Wrench 1/2-drive + Metric Hex Key Set stands out with 12 co-purchases, lift 21.31, and $211.10 average basket value contribution. Other strong cross-sell candidates include Wire Stripping Pliers + Level 24-inch (13 co-purchases, lift 20.25, $136.58) and Professional Claw Hammer 16oz + Finishing Hammer 13oz (12 co-purchases, lift 20.11, $151.63).

Takeaway: The strongest bundle opportunities are concentrated in tool + accessory and plumbing/electrical pairings, with lifts mostly in the 20x–23x range. Prioritize merchandising and checkout recommendations around the highest-value pairs first, especially the jigsaw/router, torque wrench/hex key, and GFCI/retractable cord combinations.

components.content:
Seattle is the only active location in this extract with 54,931 distinct orders spanning 2020-01-01 to 2026-12-31, so merchandising tests should be run here first. Seasonality is fairly balanced, but winter is the largest season at 14,041 orders vs 13,572 fall, 13,581 spring, and 13,737 summer—a spread of only 469 orders between peak and trough, suggesting broad demand with modest seasonal shifts.

Fall is the clearest bundle opportunity season: the strongest co-purchase pairs all show very high lift, typically 11.7x to 23.2x, even though absolute share is tiny (0.000589 to 0.000958 of orders). The highest-lift fall pair is Scrolling Jigsaw + Fixed Base Router 1-3/4 HP with 9 co-purchases, lift 23.18, and $507.45 average basket value contribution. Other strong fall pairs include Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Adjustable Wrench 10-inch (11 co-purchases, lift 22.48, $103.32) and GFCI Outlet 20-Amp + Retractable Cord Reel (9, lift 22.45, $164.30).

  • Merchandising action: place high-lift pairs together in fall endcaps and online “frequently bought together” modules, especially power tools, electrical, and plumbing adjacencies.
  • Bundle design: prioritize bundles with the highest basket contribution, not just frequency. For example, Torque Wrench 1/2-drive + Metric Hex Key Set has 12 co-purchases, lift 21.31, and $211.10 contribution; Ratcheting Screwdriver + Torque Wrench 1/2-drive reaches $438.46.
  • Promotion strategy: use seasonal attach offers in fall for tool kits and repair projects; keep discount depth modest because the lift is already strong and the pairs are naturally complementary.
  • Inventory planning: ensure paired items are in-stock together in Seattle during fall, since even low-share pairs can drive meaningful basket value when attached.

Cross-season takeaway: because the seasonal order counts are close and the product universe is stable at 424 distinct products in every season, the best approach is season-specific pairing rather than broad, year-round bundles. Focus on fall for the most aggressive bundle tests, then replicate only the top-performing pair logic into other seasons after validation.
